collection.title: Cognitive breadth expansion: attention, self, agency, time, memory, language, affect, development, comparative, collective, and machine social cognition
collection.scope: Provisional breadth records absent from the merged 249-record Noemorph corpus. This shard covers named theories, models, frameworks, and bounded empirical constructs across cognitive domains adjacent to or constitutive of research on mind and consciousness.
collection.method: Exact-name, alias, and citation-locator collision audit against catalog.json and every 2026-08-30 shard, followed by verification against DOI metadata, official proceedings, publisher records, PubMed, and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
collection.boundary_policy: Adjacent attention, timing, memory, group, and machine models explicitly state what they do and do not claim about phenomenal consciousness.
collection.attribution_policy: Claims remain local to each named record and cited authors. No inter-theory relationship, convergence, compatibility, causal synthesis, or ranking is asserted.

records.name: Guided Search Model of Visual Search
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Successive versions revise feature guidance, scene structure, search history, and target templates and should not be collapsed.
records.summary: Parallel feature processing generates priority signals that guide limited-capacity selection toward likely target locations using both salience and top-down target information.
records.boundary_note: Guided Search predicts selection and search order; it neither defines conscious visibility nor makes all selected items conscious.
records.claim_scope: Target selection and search efficiency in cluttered displays and scenes.
records.evidence_profile: Reaction-time slopes, eye movements, feature and conjunction search, and computational simulation.
open_questions: How should guidance be modeled in natural dynamic scenes?
What priority-map information is consciously reportable?

records.name: Attention Network Theory
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Alerting, orienting, and executive distinctions remain productive while later network mapping refines their independence and interaction.
records.summary: Attention comprises partially separable systems for alertness, sensory orienting, and executive conflict resolution, with characteristic brain networks and neuromodulatory influences.
records.boundary_note: The framework decomposes attention functions; no network is thereby identified as sufficient for consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Functional and neural organization of alerting, orienting, and executive attention.
records.evidence_profile: Cueing and conflict tasks, lesions, neuroimaging, electrophysiology, genetics, and development.
open_questions: How do modern control networks map onto the original executive system?
Which network operations proceed without awareness?

records.name: Attentional Blink
records.tradition: Temporal attention / rapid serial visual presentation
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: The second-target deficit is robust, but bottleneck, gating, episodic-integration, and resource accounts compete.
records.summary: When two targets occur close together in a rapid stream, report of the second is often impaired for several hundred milliseconds despite preserved processing in some conditions.
records.boundary_note: The blink is an experimental access failure, not a standalone theory of consciousness; missed targets can retain objective processing.
records.claim_scope: Temporal limits on selection, consolidation, and report of successive targets.
records.evidence_profile: Rapid serial visual presentation, lag functions, priming, electrophysiology, and model comparison.
open_questions: Which stage produces the blink across tasks?
When does an unreported target retain semantic or phenomenal processing?

records.name: Inattentional Blindness
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Nonreport of unexpected stimuli is robust, but prevalence depends on questioning, relevance, expectation, and residual processing.
records.summary: Observers occupied by a demanding task can fail to report an otherwise visible and salient unexpected object, revealing a strong dependence of reportable awareness on attentional set.
records.boundary_note: Nonreport is not automatically absence of all phenomenal experience; detection, identification, and retrospective report must be measured separately.
records.claim_scope: Awareness of unexpected stimuli while attention is engaged elsewhere.
records.evidence_profile: Unexpected-object tasks, post-trial questioning, eye tracking, and implicit-processing measures.
open_questions: Which processing survives nonreport?
How much do retrospective questioning and response criteria contribute?

records.name: Change Blindness
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Large change-detection failures are robust but do not uniquely settle the richness or format of visual representation.
records.summary: Observers can miss substantial changes across a visual disruption when attention is not directed to the changing element despite an impression of a stable, detailed scene.
records.boundary_note: Failure to detect change is not direct proof that unattended details were wholly absent from experience or memory.
records.claim_scope: Comparison and detection of scene changes across saccades, blanks, occlusion, and transients.
records.evidence_profile: Flicker, mud-splash, real-world person-change, eye-tracking, and memory-probe studies.
open_questions: What representations persist when explicit change report fails?
How do attention, memory precision, comparison, and criterion contribute?

records.name: Cue-Familiarity and Accessibility Accounts of Feeling of Knowing
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Cue familiarity and accessibility are dissociable inferential bases whose weighting varies with task and timing.
records.summary: Feeling-of-knowing judgments can derive from rapid familiarity with a cue and from the amount or strength of partial information accessed during unsuccessful retrieval rather than direct inspection of a stored target.
records.boundary_note: These accounts model metamemory judgments, not a direct conscious readout of memory contents.
records.claim_scope: Prospective judgments of later recognition or recall following retrieval failure.
records.evidence_profile: Feeling-of-knowing accuracy, cue manipulation, partial retrieval, and recognition prediction.
open_questions: How are familiarity and accessibility weighted when they conflict?
Which components enter conscious metacognitive feeling?

records.name: Two-Stage Dynamic Signal Detection Theory of Confidence
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: The joint account of choice, latency, and confidence remains active alongside alternative stopping and readout rules.
records.summary: A first accumulation stage produces a choice, then continued post-choice accumulation informs confidence, predicting systematic effects of additional time and evidence.
records.boundary_note: This is a confidence-formation theory, not a claim that confidence constitutes consciousness or is always post-decisional.
records.claim_scope: Joint distributions of choice, response time, post-choice evidence, and confidence.
records.evidence_profile: Choice-confidence experiments, latency distributions, model fits, and neural accumulation measures.
open_questions: When is confidence read out concurrently with choice?
How do post-decision evidence and error monitoring interact?

records.name: Intentional Binding Effect
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Temporal attraction between action and outcome is widely observed, but its validity as an implicit agency measure is disputed.
records.summary: A voluntary action and its effect can be perceived as closer in time than comparable involuntary or unrelated events.
records.boundary_note: Binding is a timing effect, not agency itself; causality, prediction, attention, and timing method can influence it.
records.claim_scope: Perceived temporal relation between voluntary action and anticipated or actual outcomes.
records.evidence_profile: Libet-clock judgments, interval estimates, causal and probability manipulations, and action-selection tasks.
open_questions: Which component reflects agency rather than causal binding?
How comparable are shifts across timing methods?

records.name: Multisensory Bodily Self Model
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Ownership, self-location, perspective, and agency are separable components with partially shared multisensory mechanisms.
records.summary: Visual, tactile, proprioceptive, vestibular, and interoceptive signals are integrated in body-centered frames supporting ownership, self-location, and first-person perspective.
records.boundary_note: This mechanism-level model is distinct from the catalog's generic body-ownership construct and does not reduce all selfhood to multisensory integration.
records.claim_scope: Multisensory mechanisms of ownership, self-location, and first-person perspective.
records.evidence_profile: Full-body illusions, visuotactile synchrony, vestibular manipulation, lesions, and neuroimaging.
open_questions: Which computations distinguish ownership from location and perspective?
How do interoceptive and vestibular precision alter embodiment?

records.name: Life-Story Model of Narrative Identity
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Narrative identity is studied as one personality level; developmental timing, cultural variation, and causal effects remain open.
records.summary: People construct an internalized and evolving life story integrating reconstructed past and imagined future to provide identity with temporal unity and meaning.
records.boundary_note: This is McAdams's empirical personality framework for extended narrative identity, not Schechtman's philosophical self-constitution criterion or a theory of minimal prereflective selfhood; it does not make every self-experience linguistic.
records.claim_scope: Autobiographical meaning-making, identity development, and life-story coherence.
records.evidence_profile: Narrative interviews, coding of agency and communion, longitudinal and cross-cultural studies.
open_questions: How causally do narratives shape behavior and well-being?
Which elements generalize across cultures and nonverbal populations?

records.name: Scalar Expectancy Theory
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Scalar variability is a central benchmark, while clock, memory, and decision components face competing implementations.
records.summary: Pulses accumulated during an interval are stored and compared with remembered samples; proportional noise yields Weber-like scalar variability.
records.boundary_note: SET models interval timing, not the full phenomenology or metaphysics of temporal consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Timing and discrimination of intervals, including scalar variability and memory comparison.
records.evidence_profile: Peak-interval, bisection, reproduction, animal timing, and quantitative fits.
open_questions: Which neural process implements accumulation and reference memory?
When do nonscalar patterns require alternatives?

records.name: Striatal Beat-Frequency Model of Interval Timing
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: The corticostriatal coincidence proposal remains active alongside population-clock and state-dependent models.
records.summary: Distributed cortical oscillations begin in a reproducible phase relation, and striatal neurons detect coincidence patterns corresponding to learned durations.
records.boundary_note: The model explains timing; oscillatory coincidence is not claimed to be sufficient for conscious temporal experience.
records.claim_scope: Corticostriatal encoding and learning of interval duration.
records.evidence_profile: Behavioral pharmacology, lesions, electrophysiology, timing tasks, and simulations.
open_questions: Are sufficiently stable oscillators present across relevant intervals?
How does the model generalize across contexts and timescales?

records.name: State-Dependent Network Model of Timing
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Network trajectories offer a clock-free short-interval account, while generalization across longer timescales remains unresolved.
records.summary: Elapsed time is encoded implicitly in an evolving recurrent-network state, so a later input's response depends on the trajectory initiated by earlier stimulation.
records.boundary_note: This is a neural timing model, not a theory of lived duration or conscious temporal unity.
records.claim_scope: Encoding and discrimination of short intervals through transient neural dynamics.
records.evidence_profile: In vitro dynamics, interval discrimination, recurrent-network simulation, and perturbation.
open_questions: How can transient trajectories scale to seconds and minutes?
How are context and attention read out from network state?

records.name: Chronostasis
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Action-linked temporal expansion is robust in several modalities; arousal, backdating, and continuity mechanisms differ in support.
records.summary: The first event perceived after a rapid movement, classically a saccade to a clock, can seem longer than it physically was.
records.boundary_note: Chronostasis is a local timing illusion, not evidence that consciousness literally stops or uses one central clock.
records.claim_scope: Subjective duration around saccades and other action-linked sensory transitions.
records.evidence_profile: Duration comparison, saccadic and manual-action tasks, efference manipulation, and cross-modal variants.
open_questions: How much reflects predictive remapping versus postdiction?
Which motor and sensory signals trigger temporal extension?

records.name: Dual-Process Theory of Recognition Memory
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Recollection and familiarity dissociations are extensively studied; discreteness, independence, and measurement remain disputed.
records.summary: Recognition can arise through recollection of contextual details or a graded familiarity signal without recovered context, with different behavioral and neural signatures.
records.boundary_note: Familiarity is not identical to noetic consciousness, and recollection is not a complete theory of phenomenal memory.
records.claim_scope: Recognition, remember–know judgments, recollection, familiarity, and neural dissociations.
records.evidence_profile: Receiver-operating curves, process dissociation, amnesia, aging, electrophysiology, and imaging.
open_questions: Are the processes independent or outcomes on one continuum?
How do subjective reports map to model parameters?

records.name: Constructive Episodic Simulation Hypothesis
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Memory recombination contributes to future simulation; process and neural specificity remain under study.
records.summary: Episodic memory supports imagining possible futures by flexibly extracting and recombining details from past events, with the same flexibility enabling distortion.
records.boundary_note: The hypothesis explains one function of constructive episodic memory, not all imagination, foresight, or conscious recollection.
records.claim_scope: Recombination of episodic details in personal future simulation.
records.evidence_profile: Autobiographical generation, amnesia, aging, detail coding, experimental recombination, and imaging.
open_questions: Which simulations require episodic rather than semantic support?

records.name: Scene Construction Theory
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Scene construction explains broad hippocampal involvement, while relational and predictive alternatives contest its primacy.
records.summary: The hippocampus integrates elements into spatially coherent scenes used by remembering, future imagination, navigation, and some mind wandering.
records.boundary_note: Scene construction is not equivalent to episodic memory or consciousness and does not exhaust all simulation.
records.claim_scope: Hippocampal construction of coherent scenes in memory, imagination, and navigation.
records.evidence_profile: Amnesia, imagined-scene tasks, autobiographical simulation, imaging, and coherence ratings.

records.name: Source Monitoring Framework
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Source judgments are inferential and criterion-dependent; neural and metacognitive mechanisms continue to be refined.
records.summary: Memory origins are usually inferred from perceptual, contextual, semantic, and cognitive-operation features under task-dependent criteria rather than stored as literal tags.
records.boundary_note: Source monitoring explains attribution, not all reality testing or every aspect of conscious memory.
records.claim_scope: Attribution of memories to perception, imagination, communication, and other sources.
records.evidence_profile: Source-memory tasks, false memories, aging, clinical populations, and neuroimaging.
open_questions: How are source features weighted under changing agendas?

records.name: Linguistic Relativity Hypothesis
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Modern research tests circumscribed language effects; strong linguistic determinism is not accepted.
records.summary: Habitual language properties can influence attention, categorization, memory, or reasoning, with effect size and persistence varying across domains and tasks.
records.boundary_note: Language does not rigidly determine all thought, and not every cross-linguistic difference demonstrates a cognitive effect.
records.claim_scope: Language-linked variation in color, space, time, categorization, memory, and attention.
records.evidence_profile: Cross-linguistic comparison, verbal interference, category learning, and developmental studies.
open_questions: Which effects persist without online verbal mediation?

records.name: Language of Thought Hypothesis
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Minimal compositional versions and stronger Fodorian commitments must be distinguished.
records.summary: Propositional thought involves a compositional system of mental representations whose expressions have semantically relevant constituent structure and enter causal computations.
records.boundary_note: Mentalese is not spoken language or inner speech, and the hypothesis does not itself explain phenomenal consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Representational format of propositional attitudes, reasoning, planning, and inference.
records.evidence_profile: Arguments from systematicity and productivity, computational modeling, psycholinguistics, and connectionist debate.
open_questions: Which domains require language-like representations?

records.name: Perceptual Symbol Systems
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Modal simulation is empirically productive while abstract concepts and the need for amodal structure remain disputed.
records.summary: Conceptual knowledge is represented through partial reenactments of perceptual, motor, and introspective states organized by simulators rather than exclusively arbitrary amodal symbols.
records.boundary_note: The theory does not make every simulation conscious or deny all roles for language and amodal relations.
records.claim_scope: Conceptual representation, categorization, comprehension, and grounded simulation.
records.evidence_profile: Property verification, modality switching, action-sentence compatibility, imaging, and lesions.

records.name: Deacon's Symbolic-Reference Account
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: The sign hierarchy and coevolution thesis remain influential while evolutionary details and species uniqueness are debated.
records.summary: Symbolic reference depends on learned relations among signs rather than direct resemblance or correlation alone, and symbolic culture and brain organization coevolved.

records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Multicomponent appraisal is productive, but strict appraisal sequences and emotion-pattern specificity remain under test.
records.summary: Emotion episodes emerge from recursive relevance, implication, coping, and normative appraisals that coordinate physiology, action tendency, expression, cognition, and feeling.
records.boundary_note: Appraisals need not be verbally conscious, and felt experience is only one component rather than the sole cause.

records.name: Affect Infusion Model
records.status: influential active framework · boundary conditions studied
records.status_note: Evidence supports context-dependent mood effects, while the recruitment and separation of its four processing strategies remain open to refinement.
records.summary: Transient affect is more likely to enter and color a judgment when people use constructive heuristic or substantive processing than when they retrieve a ready answer or pursue a motivated conclusion.
records.boundary_note: The model predicts affective influence on judgment under specified processing conditions; it is not a general theory of emotion, phenomenal valence, or consciousness.
records.claim_scope: When and through which information-processing strategies transient affect influences social judgments.
records.evidence_profile: Mood induction, person perception, recall, relationship judgment, impression formation, and processing-demand manipulations.

records.name: Feelings-as-Information Account
records.status: influential active framework · source-attribution effects qualified
records.status_note: Affective and experiential feelings can inform evaluation, but relevance, salience, attribution, goals, and context determine whether they are used.
records.summary: People may treat their current feelings as information about a target; when a feeling is attributed to an irrelevant source, its influence on evaluation should diminish or change.
records.boundary_note: The account concerns the informational use of felt states in judgment and processing; it does not claim that all judgments are affect-driven or explain how feelings become conscious.
records.claim_scope: How affective and other experiential feelings contribute to evaluation, judgment, and processing style through perceived informational value.
records.evidence_profile: Mood induction, weather and source-attribution manipulations, well-being judgments, processing fluency, and ease-of-retrieval paradigms.
open_questions: When do people interrogate a feeling as information rather than respond through associative priming?
How reliably do source-attribution manipulations separate informational use from demand and awareness effects?

records.name: Evaluative Space Model
records.status: active framework · mixed-affect scope and measurement debated
records.status_note: Positive and negative evaluative processes can be partly separable, although bipolar affect remains common and reports of coactivation depend on context and measurement.
records.summary: Positive and negative evaluation arise from partly separable processes rather than a single strictly bipolar mechanism, permitting reciprocal activation, uncoupled activation, coactivation, and coinhibition.
records.boundary_note: The model concerns the functional organization of positive and negative evaluation and affect; it neither identifies all emotions with two processes nor by itself explains phenomenal valence or consciousness.

records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Early competencies support constrained learning, while innateness, content, and the number of systems remain disputed.

records.name: Mentalization and Reflective-Functioning Framework

records.summary: Mentalization is understanding behavior through intentional mental states in self and others, with attachment relationships proposed to support its development and regulation.
records.boundary_note: Mentalization is broader than false-belief reasoning and not synonymous with mindreading accuracy, empathy, or introspection.

records.name: Episodic-Like What–Where–When Memory

records.summary: Nonhuman episodic-like memory is operationalized as integrated, flexible memory for what occurred, where, and when without requiring verbal evidence of subjective reliving.
records.boundary_note: Successful what–where–when performance does not establish conscious recollection, self-projection, or human-like episodic phenomenology.

records.name: Comparative Animal Theory-of-Mind Framework
records.status: active research program · scope and mechanisms contested
records.status_note: Sensitivity to perception, goals, and knowledge varies by species and paradigm; strong belief attribution remains disputed.
records.summary: Research tests whether nonhuman animals predict behavior using representations of others' perception, knowledge, goals, intentions, or beliefs rather than observable cues alone.
records.boundary_note: This is not one unified animal theory; performance must be separated from cue learning, submentalizing, and human-like explicit concepts.

records.name: Levels of Processing Framework
records.status: foundational framework · depth construct substantially revised
records.status_note: Elaborative semantic processing robustly benefits memory, while a single linear depth scale and circular definitions have been rejected.
records.summary: Memory retention depends more on the qualitative operations performed during encoding—especially elaborative semantic analysis—than on transfer into a sequence of discrete memory stores.
records.boundary_note: The framework concerns encoding and later memory, not levels of consciousness; deeper processing does not guarantee conscious recollection.
records.claim_scope: Effects of perceptual, phonological, semantic, and elaborative encoding operations on later memory.
records.evidence_profile: Incidental learning, orienting questions, recall and recognition, transfer-appropriate processing, and elaboration manipulations.
open_questions: How can processing quality be specified without circular reference to memory outcome?

records.name: Dual Coding Theory
records.status: influential active theory · code independence debated

records.summary: Cognition uses partially independent verbal and nonverbal representational systems; information encoded in both can gain additive retrieval routes and support imagery, memory, and comprehension.
records.boundary_note: Dual coding does not posit exactly two neural modules or make imagery intrinsically conscious; it is distinct from generic multimedia-design advice.

records.evidence_profile: Concreteness and imagery effects, paired associates, picture superiority, educational studies, and neuropsychology.

records.name: Two-Factor Theory of Emotion
records.status: historically foundational · original evidence and generality contested
records.status_note: Arousal-plus-interpretation remains influential, but replications and later appraisal research reject a simple universal two-step formula.
records.summary: Emotion arises through an interaction between physiological arousal and context-sensitive interpretation that labels the arousal, especially when bodily state is ambiguous.
records.boundary_note: The theory does not establish that every emotion requires undifferentiated arousal plus conscious labeling, and its original study is not decisive.
records.claim_scope: How physiological arousal and situational interpretation contribute to experienced emotion.
records.evidence_profile: Arousal manipulation, misattribution, social-context cues, replication attempts, and quantitative review.

records.name: Fuzzy-Trace Theory
aliases: fuzzy-trace theory of memory and reasoning
records.tradition: Cognitive development / memory and decision making
records.status: major active theory · representational and process claims contested
records.status_note: The verbatim–gist distinction explains broad memory and reasoning patterns, while trace independence and task-specific mechanisms remain debated.
records.summary: Experience is encoded in parallel verbatim traces preserving surface detail and gist traces preserving bottom-line meaning; gist is often more durable and increasingly preferred with development, shaping true memory, false memory, and reasoning.
records.boundary_note: Fuzzy-Trace Theory concerns representation, memory, and reasoning; gist is not intrinsically conscious, and the theory is not a general account of phenomenal consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Verbatim and gist representation in memory development, false memory, judgment, and decision making.
records.evidence_profile: True and false recognition, developmental reversals, framing, delayed testing, mathematical modeling, and neuropsychological study.
open_questions: How independently are gist and verbatim traces encoded and retrieved?

records.name: Multiprocess Framework of Prospective Memory
records.status: major active framework · process diagnostics refined
records.status_note: Evidence supports both strategic monitoring and spontaneous retrieval, while task costs are an imperfect proxy and process mixtures vary dynamically.
records.summary: Delayed intentions can be retrieved through resource-demanding monitoring for target events or through relatively spontaneous cue-driven retrieval; cue focality, context, ongoing-task demand, and individual differences shift reliance between processes.
records.boundary_note: This framework explains remembering to act in the future, not prospective phenomenal consciousness; spontaneous retrieval does not imply an unconscious intention remained continuously active.
records.claim_scope: Retrieval and execution of delayed intentions through monitoring and spontaneous cue-triggered processes.
records.evidence_profile: Event-based prospective-memory tasks, ongoing-task costs, cue focality, contextual variability, delay, and age comparisons.
open_questions: How can monitoring and spontaneous retrieval be identified without circular task-cost assumptions?
How are intentions maintained and reactivated across long naturalistic delays?

records.name: Choice Blindness
records.status: replicated experimental phenomenon · prevalence and interpretation task-sensitive
records.status_note: Undetected outcome substitutions and post-hoc reasons recur across domains, but detection depends on discrepancy, confidence, delay, and manipulation method.
records.summary: People can fail to notice that the outcome presented after a choice differs from what they selected and may nevertheless provide reasons for the manipulated outcome, revealing limits on access to choice history and preference stability.
records.boundary_note: Choice blindness does not show that all introspection is confabulation or that participants lacked an original preference; detection, compliance, memory, and demand effects require separate controls.
records.claim_scope: Awareness of mismatches between intended choices and presented outcomes and explanations generated after undetected substitutions.
records.evidence_profile: Covert outcome substitution, concurrent and retrospective detection, confidence, verbal explanation, consumer choice, and attitude-reversal paradigms.
open_questions: Which failures reflect weak memory, flexible preference, response compliance, or limited metacognitive comparison?
How do detection rates change when choices are consequential or revisitable?
